utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you followed proceedings before this Tribunal dealing with the incident at the Markale market in February 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I did follow the proceedings and I talked about that in that paragraph in an appropriate way. I wish to draw attention to the fact that there are a lot of unknowns in relation to Markale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask you for your opinion on that. The report you are referring to here, is that a report which you could establish not to have been available to this Tribunal? Because if there is any UNPROFOR report with a certain conclusion on the matter, the Chamber would not want to miss it when evaluating all of the evidence. Therefore, I asked you whether in following the proceedings whether you gained the impression that the report you are talking about here, whether that was not considered by this Tribunal in other cases?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the information I had from the press, the UNPROFOR withdrew that report already on the first day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not my question. My question was whether you think that, even if you withdraw a report, the report may still be there, whether that report is available and whether it has been available according to your knowledge. And of course if your answer is that it is a report which was not available to this Tribunal, the Chamber would urge the parties to get hold of it. Do you have any knowledge about that report which would allow any conclusions as to whether it has been available to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I have to say that I don't know if there is such a report or not. I guess there is UN documentation about it, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your only source is that you heard Mr. Walker talking about a report and stating what the content of that report was without any further knowledge about that report and its content.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have one question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought that when you talked about the Pope you gave the name of the Pope, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Pope John Paul, Pope Wojtyla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have the questions by the Bench triggered any further need for questions, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Milutinovic, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the Bench, put to you by the parties - to start with by the parties - and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you for giving me the opportunity to state my positions and views here regarding the events in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We appreciated you stating facts that are to your knowledge. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am usually hesitant to go over the time so much, but it's the last day before the -- it's the last day before the winter recess. Mr. Tieger, you asked for private session. And you -- I think you talked about one minute, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that's right. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If you would just give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I have quite a few matters still on the agenda, they are not of such urgency that we should deal with them necessarily before the recess, because we are at the point where we'll take a recess of a few weeks. The Chamber wishes everyone in this courtroom all the good wishes for the holidays, and -- whether the holidays are in December or in January, the best wishes are exactly the same also for the coming year. And having said this, we adjourn and will resume Monday, the 19th of January of 2015, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of January, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.33 p.m.,
